input.quote: If M&I and Customer are unable to agree upon the terms for renewal of this Agreement at least six (6) months prior to the expiration of the Term, then Customer may, at its option, renew this Agreement for one (1) twelve month period at the then-current terms and conditions of this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 is the only extension mechanic (Section 2.1 and the "Term" definition simply cross-refer to it, and no other provision extends the Term). There is no automatic renewal: the Agreement expires at the end of the eight-year Term unless the parties affirmatively agree renewal terms, so renewal requires mutual written agreement and the preferred position's conditional automatic-renewal elements (12-month renewal term, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder) are not triggered. Customer bears no non-renewal notice window and cannot be locked in; the only unilateral extension right runs in our favour (Customer's option to extend for a single twelve-month period), and it is expressly "at the then-current terms and conditions," so no renewal price increase is permitted and the CPI/3% cap element is likewise not engaged. M&I's 18-month proposal obligation and Customer's 6-month response step benefit Customer's planning and do not create an exit hurdle. This sits at the preferred position; no redline proposed.
